reuse.why: All four steps go through the existing getDateWithSkippedWeekend, which every caller (getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the new getDatesInRange, schedule-template) uses for daily skipping, holidays and MM-DD holidays.

duplication.why: Weekend/holiday rules are defined once (isHoliday, isWeekendOrHoliday) and schedule-template's two copies collapse into one closure; only the 'how many occurrences to look ahead' sizing is restated three different ways.

placement.why: Date rules live in shared/schedules.ts, the new handler sits in schedules/app.ts next to get-upcoming-dates, and the config type gains the field.

scope.why: Focused on the four requests; the schedule-template rewrite into getAdjustedDate is a justified consolidation of code it had to touch.

maintainability.why: One function owns the date adjustment with clear helpers, though returning null for daily skips and the ad hoc look-ahead windows (searchWindow, count*7, shiftDays) are things a maintainer must keep in sync.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every adjusted-date path calls getDateWithSkippedWeekend; none re-tests weekends or holidays itself.

disguised_duplication.where: Look-ahead sizing for runs of weekend/holiday days appears as getWeekendSearchWindow in shared/schedules.ts, count * 7 + holidays * 7 in getUpcomingDates and 2 * (holidays + 1) shiftDays in getDatesInRange.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains frequency and holidays parameters and a daily -> null branch; all call sites route through it, so the growth reflects real variation rather than drift.
